newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Fipe inflation at 1.23 pct - Fipe.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Fipe inflation at 1.23 pct - Fipe.

text.p: Brazil's inflation as measured by the Economic Research Institute (Fipe) was 1.23 percent in January, up from 0.17 percent in December, a Fipe official said.
Juarez Rizzieri, president of Fipe, said a rise in food prices, transport and education costs accelerated the price index, which measures costs in the city of Sao Paulo.

Food prices rose 1.51 percent in the period, while transport prices were up 2.75 percent due to an increase in the cost of gasoline and education costs increased 8.83 percent due to school enrolments.
Rizzieri said he expected the February Fipe index to be around 0.5 percent, saying January was an exceptional month with probably the highest monthly inflation rate to be seen in 1997.
He gave the following breakdown of the Fipe weighted index for the period.
- Food 1.51 pct rise in the period
The Fipe index is calculated by the University of Sao Paulo, which releases inflation figures at weekly intervals.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
